scenes.image: A long candlelit Thanksgiving table seen from the end, a family seated, one carved chair empty with a full place setting.
lines: [low, deliberate] Every Thanksgiving, Evelyn Whitmore set the table for her family. [pause] This year, she set one extra place.
sfx: Thanksgiving dinner, cutlery, glasses clinking, quiet conversation in a large dining room

scenes.image: Michael at the table, frowning at the empty chair beside him.
lines: [light, puzzled] Mom... why is there an extra chair?

scenes.image: Diane glancing around the table with a tight smile.
Richard at the head of the table, setting down his glass very slowly.
Claire leaning toward her grandmother, curious and uneasy.
lines: [gently] Grandma? Who are we waiting for?
sfx: A silver fork dropping onto a china plate

scenes.image: Michael staring at his mother, half laughing.
Evelyn at the table in candlelight, hands folded, looking straight at her husband.
lines: [slow, every word weighed] The daughter your grandfather made me give away... forty years ago.
sfx: Sudden silence in a large room, a clock ticking

scenes.image: Richard rigid at the head of the table; Diane staring at her mother, stunned.
lines: [shaken] Mom, what are you talking about?

scenes.image: Michael leaning toward Evelyn, voice dropping.
lines: [too quickly] You never had another daughter.

scenes.image: Richard's face hard in the candlelight.
lines: [quiet fury] No, Richard. I've spent forty years embarrassing myself... pretending she never existed.

scenes.image: The heavy front door of the estate from inside, a silhouette behind its frosted glass.
sfx: An old deep doorbell chiming through a large house

scenes.image: Claire half rising from her chair; Richard pointing at her.
Claire opening the heavy front door; Anna on the step in a navy coat, autumn wind behind her.
lines: [breath catching, almost a whisper] Oh my God. [pause] You have her eyes.
sfx: Heavy front door opening, autumn wind and leaves
scenes.motion: the door swings open and wind lifts Anna's scarf

scenes.image: Evelyn walking into the foyer, reaching out both hands to Anna.
Richard appearing in the dining room doorway behind them, blocking it.
Close-up of Anna looking past Evelyn, straight at Richard, very calm.
lines: [calm, measured] Actually, Mr. Whitmore... before I leave, there's something your family should know. [pause] I've been inside this house before. [pause] You opened the door.

scenes.image: Close-up of Richard, the color draining from his face.
lines: [slow] To understand what she meant... we have to go back three weeks. [pause] To a phone call Evelyn had waited forty years for.

scenes.image: Three weeks earlier: Evelyn alone in the big kitchen in the morning, answering an old wall phone.
sfx: Old landline phone ringing in a quiet kitchen

scenes.image: Anna at her small kitchen table, phone at her ear, an old yellowed envelope in her other hand.
lines: [taking a breath] My name is Anna Morgan.

scenes.image: Evelyn gripping the edge of the counter, frozen.
lines: [faint] I'm sorry... could you repeat that?
[gently] Anna Morgan. [pause] I believe you may be my biological mother.

scenes.image: Close-up of Evelyn's hand trembling on the phone cord.
lines: I found an old letter among my adoptive mother's things.

scenes.image: Close-up of an old handwritten letter on yellowed paper, addressed 'To my baby, Anna'.
lines: [reading, voice soft] I did not leave you because I didn't love you.

scenes.image: Evelyn sliding down to sit on a kitchen stool, hand over her mouth.
sfx: A sharp breath catching, then silence

scenes.image: Anna pressing the letter to her chest, eyes filling.
lines: [crying softly] I've waited forty years to hear someone say that.

scenes.image: Evelyn wiping her eyes, glancing toward the kitchen door.
lines: [urgent, low] Anna, there's so much I need to tell you.
[steadier] Then tell me why you gave me away.

scenes.image: No people visible. An empty kitchen doorway from inside the quiet kitchen, only the long dark shadow of a man falling across the hallway floor beyond it.
lines: [very quiet] Because the man who made me do it... is still living in my house.

scenes.image: Days later: Diane arranging place cards on the long dining table, Evelyn folding napkins.
lines: [brisk, managing] Mother, the caterers arrive at four on Thanksgiving.
And please don't invite any more of your old friends.

scenes.image: Evelyn calmly folding a napkin.
Diane holding a place card with the name of the governor's wife, eyebrows raised.
lines: [dry] More important than the governor's wife?

scenes.image: Evelyn setting the napkin down, looking at her daughter.
lines: [tired] Diane, when did Thanksgiving become a networking event?
[flat] When Michael started running for district attorney.

scenes.image: Mother and daughter facing each other across the table.
lines: [pointed] So the entire family must pretend to be perfect?

scenes.image: Richard walking in, reading glasses in hand, eyeing the place cards.
Evelyn meeting her husband's eyes without blinking.
lines: [evenly] Someone I should have invited years ago.

scenes.image: Richard holding the door open to the hall, jaw tight.
lines: [quiet, controlled] We need to talk. [pause] Privately.

scenes.image: Richard shutting the heavy study door, turning on his silver-haired wife Evelyn under the green desk lamp; nobody else in the room.
lines: [low, furious] Tell me you haven't contacted that woman.
sfx: Heavy study door closing, rain on the window

scenes.image: Evelyn alone by the rainy study window, arms folded, the green desk lamp beside her.
lines: [cutting] You haven't spoken it in forty years.

scenes.image: Richard pouring a whiskey, not looking at her.
lines: [dismissive] Because we agreed to put it behind us.
[voice rising] You agreed. [pause] I cried until I couldn't breathe.

scenes.image: The two of them facing each other across the dark study.
lines: [hard] From a scandal that would have destroyed everything.

scenes.image: Richard swirling his glass, contemptuous.
lines: She hasn't asked for a penny.

scenes.image: Evelyn stepping closer, eyes bright.
Richard leaning on the desk, voice dropping to a threat.
lines: [very low] If you bring her into this house... you will regret it.

scenes.image: Close-up of Evelyn, tears standing in her eyes, chin up.
lines: [quiet, steady] I've regretted something every Thanksgiving for forty years.
[breaking softly] Setting a table without my daughter.

scenes.image: Anna alone at a corner table in a rainy coffee shop, both hands around a cup, watching the door.
lines: [soft] They met for the first time in a coffee shop in Boston. [pause] Anna had arrived forty minutes early.
sfx: Quiet coffee shop, espresso machine, rain outside

scenes.image: Evelyn sitting down across from Anna, neither knowing what to do with their hands.
lines: [quiet] I thought you might look at me... and change your mind.

scenes.image: Evelyn looking at Anna as if memorizing her face.
lines: [aching] No. And that's my greatest regret.

scenes.image: Anna turning her cup slowly.
Anna reaching into her bag.
lines: Before she died, she told me she'd kept something from me.
sfx: A photograph sliding across a wooden table

scenes.image: Close-up of a faded 1980s photograph on the table: a young dark-haired woman in a hospital bed holding a newborn wrapped in a pink blanket.
Anna alone in frame at the coffee shop table, her composure cracking, an empty chair behind her.
lines: [voice catching] I thought you never wanted me.
[urgent, tender] Anna, I held you for three days.

scenes.image: Flashback, forty years ago: a young dark-haired mother in a hospital bed cradling a newborn, gray winter light, the door opening behind her.
lines: [remembering, hollow] Then Richard came to the hospital... with an attorney.
sfx: Soft hospital room tone, a door opening
scenes.motion: the young mother looks up from the baby as the door opens

scenes.image: Evelyn staring at the photo, back in that room.
lines: [flat with old pain] That if I kept you... I'd lose Michael and Diane.

scenes.image: Anna leaning in, disbelieving.
lines: [quietly] He said he'd make sure I never saw them again.

scenes.image: Close-up of Evelyn, ashamed.
lines: [low] I was thirty-four, frightened, and I didn't have a dollar of my own.

scenes.image: Anna's eyes hardening slightly, hurt.
lines: [sharper] You could have found me later.

scenes.image: Close-up of Anna alone in frame, tears spilling over, the rainy window behind her.
lines: [breaking] Then why did nobody ever come?

scenes.image: Evelyn reaching across the table and taking Anna's hand.
lines: [soft] You can call me Evelyn. [pause] But I hope... someday... you'll call me Mom.
[a wet half laugh] Let's start with Evelyn.

scenes.image: A week later in Anna's small apartment: Evelyn setting a worn shoe box on the kitchen table.
sfx: Small apartment, a box lid lifted, papers rustling

scenes.image: No faces visible. Overhead close-up of a shoe box on a kitchen table overflowing with handwritten letters, birthday cards and Christmas cards, all addressed to Anna, two pairs of hands, one older, lifting them out.
scenes.motion: hands slowly lift a stack of old letters out of the shoe box

scenes.image: Anna reading one card, her hand over her mouth.
Evelyn shaking her head slowly.
lines: [firm] I did. [pause] Through the adoption agency. They wrote back that contact wasn't permitted.
[stunned] My parents said nobody ever contacted them.

scenes.image: Close-up of Evelyn's face going still and cold.
Anna setting the card down, hesitating.
lines: [quiet] I came to your house. When I was sixteen.

scenes.image: Flashback: a sixteen-year-old girl with long brown hair in a rain jacket standing on the wet stone steps of the estate, ringing the bell.
lines: [remembering] My father found an old address. I took two buses in the rain. I wanted to know if it was yours.
sfx: Rain on stone steps, a doorbell
scenes.motion: the teenage girl reaches up and rings the bell in the rain

scenes.image: Flashback: the front door opening; a tall man in his fifties with dark-gray hair in the doorway, looking down at the teenage girl.
Anna looking down at her hands.
lines: [steady but hurt] He said you knew about me. [pause] He said you'd paid him to make sure I never came back.

scenes.image: Evelyn with both hands pressed to her chest, devastated.
lines: [fierce through tears] I never said that.

scenes.image: Anna reaching for an old envelope at the bottom of her bag.
lines: [deliberate] Because I still have what he gave me.

scenes.image: Close-up of an old personal check, never cashed, five thousand dollars, a bold signature 'Richard Whitmore'.
lines: [quiet] He handed me this. At the door.

scenes.image: Evelyn staring at the check.
Close-up of Anna, calm and wounded.
lines: [quiet, steady] I wanted a mother. [pause] Not money.

scenes.image: Evelyn holding the old check in trembling fingers.
lines: [low, shaking] I knew he could be cruel.

scenes.image: Close-up of Evelyn, anger rising through the grief.
lines: [voice hardening] But I never imagined he'd look into my daughter's face... and tell her I didn't want her.

scenes.image: Evelyn folding the check back into its envelope and handing it to Anna with resolve.
lines: [iron] For once, Richard doesn't get to decide who belongs in this family.

scenes.image: Michael alone in his law office at night, campaign posters reading 'Whitmore for D.A.' stacked against the wall, phone buzzing.
sfx: Phone vibrating on a desk, quiet office at night

scenes.image: Close-up of Michael, utterly still.
Richard in his dark study, phone at his ear, frowning.
Michael loosening his tie, leaning back in his chair.
lines: [matter-of-fact] She contacted me two years ago.

scenes.image: Richard setting down his whiskey.
lines: I told her the family wasn't interested.

scenes.image: Michael spinning a pen, avoiding his own reflection in the dark window.
lines: [casual] I also told her Mother was in poor health. [pause] Too confused to understand who she was.
[cool] Because I didn't want her showing up.

scenes.image: Richard pacing in the study.
Michael sitting forward, worried for the first time.
lines: [tense] We're not fine. [pause] She has documents.

scenes.image: Close-up of Richard, eyes narrowed.
lines: [exasperated] Dad, I'm in the middle of an election campaign.
[icy] Then you'd better make sure this family doesn't become tomorrow's headline.

scenes.image: Thanksgiving morning: Claire on the dim upstairs landing, stopping outside a half-open door, lamplight and voices spilling out.
lines: [urgent, hushed, from inside] Diane, listen to me.
sfx: Old house hallway, muffled voices behind a door

scenes.image: Through the gap in the door: Michael and Diane arguing in low voices in a guest bedroom.
Michael pacing, rubbing his forehead.
lines: [sharp] From a woman who could destroy this family.

scenes.image: Diane staring at her brother.
lines: [low] Think about what happens if she starts asking questions.

scenes.image: Close-up of Michael, voice dropping further.
lines: [barely audible] The adoption. Dad's business. [pause] The money.

scenes.image: Michael spinning toward the door.
Claire in the doorway, arms crossed, chin up.
lines: [forced calm] Claire. How much did you hear?

scenes.image: Michael pointing a finger at his daughter.
Close-up of Claire, eyes bright with anger.
lines: [quiet, devastating] That's what everyone in this family says... whenever they're hiding something.

scenes.image: Thanksgiving afternoon in the steamy kitchen: Evelyn basting the turkey, Claire hovering at her elbow.
sfx: Busy kitchen, oven door, sizzling, a timer ticking

scenes.image: Claire biting her lip, then blurting it out.
lines: She contacted him two years ago.

scenes.image: Evelyn slowly setting down the baster.
Close-up of Evelyn, staring at nothing.
lines: [remembering] I called him on my birthday that year.

scenes.image: Evelyn gripping the edge of the counter, voice cracking.
lines: [cracking] I told him I'd been dreaming about a little girl again. [pause] He said I should stop living in the past.

scenes.image: Claire wiping her eyes.
lines: What are you going to do?

scenes.image: Evelyn taking one extra china plate down from a high cabinet.
lines: [a small, dangerous smile] No. [pause] That's where it begins.
scenes.motion: she lifts an extra china plate down from the cabinet

scenes.image: Evelyn at the kitchen phone, speaking quietly with her back to the door.
lines: [low] Before dinner, Evelyn made one more phone call. [pause] To a man she hadn't spoken to in forty years.

scenes.image: The long Thanksgiving table at dusk, candles lit, the family seated, the empty chair waiting.
lines: [measured] Which brings us back to Thanksgiving dinner.
[impatient] Let's eat before it gets cold.

scenes.image: Michael raising his glass toward his father.
lines: [smooth] Dad, perhaps you should say grace.

scenes.image: Evelyn with her eyes closed and hands folded at the candlelit table, everyone's heads bowed.
lines: [slow, deliberate] Dear God, thank you for bringing this family together. [pause] For the food on our table. For the people we love. [pause] And for the chance to tell the truth... before it's too late.

scenes.image: Richard opening his eyes and staring hard at his wife.
The front door from inside, the doorbell button glowing, Claire hurrying across the foyer.
lines: [low] And the conversation went exactly as Evelyn knew it would. [pause] Until the doorbell rang.

scenes.image: Evelyn leading Anna, coat now off, into the candlelit dining room, every head turning.
lines: [warm, proud] Everyone. This is Anna. Come in, sweetheart.

scenes.image: Richard rising from the head of the table.
lines: [without turning] You don't get to decide that.

scenes.image: Michael standing, hands raised, his campaign smile on.
lines: [reasonable, tight] Mom, can we please discuss this privately?

scenes.image: Anna and Michael looking at each other across the table, recognition in both faces.
Anna turning to Diane, voice steady.
lines: [calm] He told me our mother didn't want to see me.

scenes.image: Close-up of Anna, unflinching.
lines: [quiet, precise] You said she was too sick to understand who I was.
[defensive] I was trying not to upset her.

scenes.image: Evelyn standing at her place, trembling with anger.
lines: [low, shaking] You let me believe my daughter was lost to me.
[breaking] You watched me cry every single birthday.

scenes.image: Michael looking down at his plate.
lines: [weak] I didn't know what to do.
[cold] You could have told me the truth.

scenes.image: Anna facing Richard across the length of the table.
lines: [gentle, to the table] I didn't come here to take anyone's place.

scenes.image: Richard leaning on the table with both fists.
lines: [cold] And what exactly do you expect from us?

scenes.image: Close-up of Anna, voice dropping, every word deliberate.
lines: [slow, quiet] To why you told a sixteen-year-old girl... that her mother had paid to make her disappear.
sfx: Gasps around a table, then silence

scenes.image: Close-up of the old uncashed check laid on the white tablecloth between the turkey and the candles.
sfx: Paper placed on a wooden table

scenes.image: Richard not looking at the check.
lines: [steady] You handed it to me at your front door. In the rain.

scenes.image: Diane staring at the check, then at her father.
Anna's voice rising for the first time.
lines: [rising] I was sixteen. I wasn't confused about wanting to meet my mother.
[without looking at him] I wasn't talking to you.

scenes.image: Richard sitting back, playing the generous man.
lines: [magnanimous] I gave you money because I felt sorry for you.
[sharp] You told me never to come back.

scenes.image: Evelyn slowly turning to her husband.
lines: [voice breaking] That terrible chapter was our daughter.

scenes.image: Richard smiling thinly.
lines: [cold] Evelyn, you agreed to the adoption.

scenes.image: Anna glancing toward the foyer.
lines: [calm] Then maybe we should hear the version your old attorney remembers.
sfx: Doorbell ringing again through a big house

scenes.image: Peter Hale stepping into the dining room doorway in a tweed jacket, holding an old leather document box.
sfx: Footsteps on hardwood, a door closing
scenes.motion: he steps into the doorway holding an old leather box

scenes.image: Peter standing at the end of the table, everyone staring.
Richard rising, pointing to the door.
lines: [furious, controlled] This is a private family dinner.

scenes.image: Peter setting the leather box down on the sideboard.
lines: [steady] Evelyn asked me to explain something that should have been explained decades ago.

scenes.image: Close-up of Peter, glasses in hand.
lines: [measured] Forty years ago, Richard instructed me to prepare the papers for Anna's adoption.

scenes.image: Evelyn looking at Peter, steeling herself.
Peter speaking slowly to the whole table.
lines: [plain, heavy] Richard told Evelyn that if she refused, he'd go after custody of Michael and Diane. [pause] And use every legal advantage he had to make sure she lost.

scenes.image: Michael leaning forward, lawyer mode.
lines: [calm] I kept notes of every meeting. Dated. In my own hand.

scenes.image: Peter nodding slowly.
lines: [honest] They can. I won't pretend my notes are a court judgment. [pause] But I was in that hospital room. And I remember what was said.

scenes.image: Close-up of Evelyn, forty years of hurt in her eyes.
lines: [quiet, raw] Then why didn't you help me?

scenes.image: Peter looking down, ashamed.
lines: [heavy] Because I was young, ambitious... and more worried about keeping a powerful client than doing the right thing.

scenes.image: Peter opening the old leather box; inside, bundles of unopened envelopes tied with string.
lines: [slow] There's one more thing. [pause] The adoption agency never refused your letters, Evelyn. [pause] Richard had them forwarded to my office.
sfx: An old box lid opening, paper rustling
scenes.motion: he lifts the lid, revealing bundles of old unopened envelopes

scenes.image: Close-up of stacks of yellowed, unopened envelopes in a box, each addressed in the same handwriting: 'For Anna'.
lines: [soft, devastating] Forty years of birthday cards. [pause] Forty years of Christmas letters. [pause] Every one of them... still sealed.

scenes.image: Evelyn staring at the box, a hand over her heart, then turning to her husband.
lines: [barely a whisper] You kept them. [pause] All this time... you kept them from her.

scenes.image: Anna lifting one envelope, her own name on it in her mother's handwriting, tears falling.
lines: [a broken whisper] They're addressed to me.
[gently] I should have given them to you years ago. [pause] I'm sorry.

scenes.image: Michael standing, trying to take control of the room.
lines: [loud, lawyerly] Fine. Dad behaved terribly forty years ago. [pause] What does any of that have to do with today?

scenes.image: Richard's hand tightening on his glass.
Peter taking a bound document from the box.
lines: [measured] Richard's father set up a family trust before he died.
The trust provided for Richard's children.

scenes.image: Michael with a confident smile.
Close-up of Anna, realizing.
lines: [slowly] I was born before your grandfather died.

scenes.image: Diane turning to her father; Richard avoiding her eyes.
lines: [stiff] She wasn't raised in this family.
[calm] That doesn't automatically decide whether she qualifies under the trust.

scenes.image: Michael's smile gone.
lines: [tight] You're saying Anna could have a claim?
I'm saying the original documents need an independent review.

scenes.image: Anna raising her hands, shaking her head.
lines: [earnest] I didn't know about any trust until last month.
[triumphant sneer] There it is. [pause] The money.

scenes.image: Close-up of Anna, quiet and sure.
lines: [quiet] No. [pause] There it is. The reason you were so determined to erase me.

scenes.image: Evelyn turning slowly to Richard.
lines: [very quiet] Richard. Did you hide her... because of the trust?
[cold, unrepentant] I did what was necessary.

scenes.image: Husband and wife facing each other across the candlelit table.
Close-up of Anna, a single tear, voice barely above a whisper.
Michael turning to his mother, spreading his hands.
lines: [pleading, reasonable] Mom, you can't seriously believe these people.

scenes.image: Evelyn looking at her son as if seeing a stranger.
lines: [icy] One is my daughter. The other was your father's attorney.

scenes.image: Anna meeting Michael's eyes calmly.
lines: [calm] I haven't asked Evelyn for anything.

scenes.image: Claire standing up at her place.
Michael staring at his daughter in disbelief.
lines: You knew about Anna two years ago.

scenes.image: Close-up of Claire, scared but determined, phone in her hand.
lines: [quiet] But there's something you haven't told Grandma.
[steady] I saw the email you sent your campaign lawyer.

scenes.image: Michael going pale.
lines: [cutting him off] You asked whether an undisclosed family member could complicate the trust.

scenes.image: Evelyn turning slowly toward her son.
lines: [too fast] It was a hypothetical question.

scenes.image: Diane staring at her brother, betrayed.
lines: [stunned] You knew there might be money involved?

scenes.image: Anna rising slowly from her chair.
